item.title: The Connect: Community Jam — Tue Oct 6, 8:00 PM — The One Stop
item.description:
Introducing The Connect: a weekly community jam at The One Stop curated by Women to the Front on Tuesdays, 8-11pm.
Asheville Music Hall The One Stop has a long history of being a place where musicians come together. The Connect is about continuing that spirit while helping create something new. This weekly jam aims to be a welcoming, respectful space where professional musicians, rising artists, and everyone in between can come together to collaborate, connect, and learn from each other.
Each week will feature a thoughtfully curated group of musicians who will start the night with a short set and then open the night to a jam. The goal is to build community across different generations, backgrounds, genres, and levels of experience. We are committed to creating an environment where everyone can feel safe, respected, and encouraged to attend.
Come play, come listen, come make some new friends, and help us reconnect with Asheville’s music community.
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: Ask About Our Featured Listings — Wed Oct 7 — LiveMusicAsheville.com
item.description:
Established in February 2019, LiveMusicAsheville.com now reaches thousands of people every week actively searching for live music in the Asheville area. Roughly 60% of our traffic comes from Google Search as we dominate the top of the results for queries such as “Asheville live music” & “live music Asheville”. Meanwhile our direct traffic is experiencing explosive growth, proving more locals are now using us as their go-to music calendar. Our free listings include just the basics of Who’s Playin’ Where & When. Our Featured Listings really stand out among the dozens of events on the calendar every day. While we update every Wednesday for the following Friday thru Thursday, these Featured Listings are published much sooner and include your picture or poster, a description of the event and the venue, website/ticket links and a Google map. We also share these events on our social media stories to help further promote your show.
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: Public Talk: Mimicking Bioinorganic Chemistry to Tackle Greenhouse Gas Emissions — Wed Oct 7, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Alex Heyer, Ph. D. will discuss his research on the chemistry of methane, a potent greenhouse gas, and how novel approaches using copper-containing zeolites could help remove it. The talk in the Mullen & James Humanities Lecture Hall will explore how scientists can mimic bioinorganic chemistry to better understand methane reactivity and develop new strategies for addressing greenhouse gas emissions. This event is free and open to the public.

item.title: Lea and Heffernan of Wheelchair Sports Camp — Fri Oct 9, 3:00 PM
item.description:
Gaelynn Lea and Kalyn Rose Heffernan of Wheelchair Sports Camp will visit UNC Asheville for an afternoon talk and evening performance. At 3 p.m., Lea and Heffernan will discuss disability culture, access, and activism, sharing their experiences as artists and advocates working to make the arts more inclusive. At 6 p.m., Wheelchair Sports Camp will take the stage for a free performance. Lea, winner of NPR Music’s Tiny Desk Contest, is an accomplished violinist, songwriter, composer, and disability advocate who has performed around the world and composed the score for Macbeth on Broadway. Wheelchair Sports Camp, led by wheelchair-using rapper Kalyn Rose Heffernan, blends hip-hop, humor, and high-energy performance. The Denver-based band has expanded its work beyond music into performance art, museums, theater, film, and activism. Both events are free and open to the public and will take place in the Blue Ridge Room of the Highsmith Student Union.

item.title: "Lost Ground: America's Landslide Crisis" Film Screening — Wed Oct 14, 6:30 PM
item.description:
UNC Asheville will be screening the recent documentary “Lost Ground: America’s Landslide Crisis” in Mullen & James Humanities Hall. The screening is to be followed by a panel discussion and Q&A moderated by the director, WCNC’s investigative reporter Nate Morabito. The panelists include:
Paige Ambord and Caitlin Meagher, faculty in the Department of Sociology and Anthropology and who are featured in the film for their work on landslide survivors post-Helene Jackie Langille, an expert on landslide geography in the Department of Environmental Science.
This important film exposes the extent of landslide damage during Helene, and raises awareness of landslide risks, two years after that devastating event.

item.title: 9:15 Contemplative Service — Sun Oct 18, 9:15 AM — *1 Sanctuary
item.description:
At 9:15 AM, we have a 40-45 minute Contemplative Worship Service. This service invites participants into a reflective, more meditative space, and includes silence, beautiful recorded music and videos, and opportunities for sharing. It also features the sermon and theme which will be the focus in the second service at 11:15 AM. This service is not livestreamed., and it include childcare but not a full religious education program. This service will be particularly good if you need quiet in order to hear well or focus, would prefer a little more space around you, or seek a more contemplative communal experience. Between services, at 10 am we will have coffee hour and special programs. Whether you come to the early service or the later service, we encourage you to consider arriving at 10 am for coffee, conversation, and special programs including conversations with the Board, or Minister & lay-led justice or adult education offerings.

item.title: Shut Up & Write - South Asheville — Sun Oct 25, 10:30 AM
item.description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina Coworking for writers in your area! Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.
Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.
Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!
A note about the format We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

item.title: MST Walker Knob Overlook/Balsam Gap - Route 128, 8.5mi, 2,300ft FITNESS HIKE — Wed Oct 7, 9:30 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group Most of the hike is forecast to be through "high color," with the top of Blackstop Knob at "peak color." Courtesy of Hurricane Helene, Blackstop Knob now offers a great view of the west side of the Mt. Mitchell ridge, which should be at "peak color." Current weather forecast looks perfect.
Out and back hike. The trail elevates quickly and then undulates along a ridge of the Black Mountain chain. Expect to see lots of moss, ferns, and fungi. Some of the trail is rocky; some is soft moss and pine needle carpet.
Asheville car poolers will meet at the Folk Art Center lower parking lot at 8:45am. Weavervillians should arrange their own carpool. The hike will start at the Walker Knob Overlook on the Parkway at 9:30am. Please let the hike leader know if you intend to carpool from the Folk Art Center. Any rain cancellation or venue change will be made by 7:00.
